note: Scripture source: the Indian Revised Version (IRV Hindi, CC BY-SA 4.0), parsed from the ebible mirror's USX (gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/hin_irv), all 66 books (31,104 verses), with notes, section headings, acrostic/speaker paras, cross-reference spans and the IRV's trailing cross-reference parentheses stripped. Translators looked up every quotation, cited or not, in that verse file and pasted the wording.

Derived by measurement: a row is mined only when the translator reported the quotation verbatim or partial-verbatim AND its block contains a 30-character run of that verse, or a 10+ character span the translator reported placing that is a substring of both the verse and the block (punctuation and quotation marks stripped). Translator-flagged self-rendered rows stay self_rendered (demotion only); ranges over three verses keep only the verses actually present. 238 of 421 rows mined.

Manual demotions: Ezekiel 33:8 (ch.13) — the IRV text reads 'लेखा में तुझी', an apparent typo, and the translator substituted 'मैं' from the parallel Ezekiel 3:18, so the wording is not byte-for-byte IRV; Colossians 3:11 (ch.4) — Baxter makes God the subject where the IRV has मसीह, and the translator kept परमेश्वर.

IRV/KJV divergences flagged by the translators (self-rendered): 2 Cor 5:11 'terrors of the Lord' (IRV has only 'fear'); Rev 15:3 'King of saints' (IRV 'युग-युग के राजा'); 2 Kings 8:13 Hazael's indignant 'Is thy servant a dog' (IRV reads as modesty); Acts 20:24 'none of these things move me … with joy' (absent from IRV); Isa 49:4-5 'though Israel be not gathered' (a reading IRV lacks); Lev 19:17 'not suffer sin upon him' (IRV's last clause differs); 2 Sam 12:12 'before the sun' (IRV 'दिन दुपहरी'); Rom 10:17 'preaching of the word' kept where IRV has 'मसीह के वचन'.

Conventions: quotations set in curly single marks ‘ ’ throughout (the English is curly-single with 24 stray straight doubles, several mispaired as ‘…" — all set ‘…’; no straight marks in the Hindi); minister-to-minister address तुम, vocative भाइयो; the minister speaking to a parishioner in Baxter's sample dialogues uses आप; minister सेवक, pastor पासबान, flock झुण्ड, parish पल्ली, catechizing प्रश्नोत्तर-शिक्षा, conversion मन-फिराव (हृदय-परिवर्तन only where repentance and conversion stand side by side), pulpit प्रचार-मंच, divine (theologian) धर्मविज्ञानी; book title सुधारित पासबान as already used by the shipped hi Baxter editions.
AI translation (ai_unreviewed), fanned out over 22 translator agents by part; reconciled for terms across parts afterwards.
